hook.line: Mariana is recording a podcast and wants her listeners to catch the one detail that matters. In English you lean on the word with your voice. Spanish often drops a small pinpointing word right in front of it.
hook.es: Precisamente por eso volví a Bogotá.
hook.en: That's exactly why I came back to Bogotá.

examples.en: That's exactly why we decided to wait.
It has everything, even a pool.

examples.es: Me gusta caminar, sobre todo por la mañana.
examples.en: I like walking, especially in the morning.
Specifically, we need two more people.

examples.es: Aquí todos toman tinto, incluso Hernando.
examples.en: Everyone here drinks black coffee, even Hernando.

examples.es: Me encanta el café, sobre todo el café de Rosa.
examples.en: I love coffee, especially Rosa's café.

rule:
Four small words put a spotlight on whatever comes right after them.

*Precisamente*: for exactly that reason, or exactly this one. *Precisamente por eso* = that's exactly why.
*Concretamente*: specifically, to name the detail.
*Sobre todo*: especially, the best case among several.
*Incluso*: even, the surprising extreme.

Put the word just before the thing you are lighting up. English moves your voice. Spanish moves a word, so the listener hears the point even in a text message.
smallPrint: Teachers call these *adverbios de foco*, focus adverbs: they point at one part of the sentence.

options: Even Hernando came.
Especially Hernando came.
Only Hernando came.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence (I like walking, especially in the morning): Me gusta caminar, ___ por la mañana. (sobre todo / incluso)
yourTurn.answer: Me gusta caminar, sobre todo por la mañana.
accept: Me gusta caminar sobre todo por la mañana.
yourTurn.why: Picking the best case out of several is *sobre todo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence (Everyone came, even Hernando): Vinieron todos, ___ Hernando. (incluso / precisamente)
yourTurn.why: Hernando is the surprising extreme, so *incluso*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: That's exactly why we decided to wait.
yourTurn.why: *Precisamente* sits before *por eso* to point at the reason.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Specifically, we need two more people.
Type in Spanish: It has everything, even a pool.
accept: Tiene de todo, incluso una piscina.
yourTurn.why: A pool is the surprising extra, so *incluso*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it stronger with a word that means especially: Me gusta el café.
yourTurn.answer: Me gusta el café, sobre todo por la mañana.
accept: Me gusta el café, sobre todo el café de Rosa.
Sobre todo me gusta el café de Rosa.
yourTurn.why: *Sobre todo* needs a thing or time after it to spotlight.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Everyone knows it, even the parrot.
yourTurn.answer: Todos lo saben, incluso el loro.
accept: Todos lo saben incluso el loro.
yourTurn.why: The unexpected one at the end comes right after *incluso*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me gusta caminar, incluso por la mañana.
pitfalls.right: Me gusta caminar, sobre todo por la mañana.
pitfalls.why: *Incluso* says even, as if mornings were surprising; for your favourite moment, use *sobre todo*.
For that's exactly why, Spanish says *precisamente por eso*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hasta todos vinieron, sobre todo Hernando, que nunca sale.
pitfalls.right: Vinieron todos, incluso Hernando, que nunca sale.
pitfalls.why: A surprise is *incluso*; *sobre todo* would just mean he came more than the rest.

personal: Say one thing you love and one place or time you love it most. Use *sobre todo*.
